chapter: Asides on character, a piano and Oslo
title: Judging men by their actions and choosing his own bandsmen
summary: Briggs says he judges people as men by what they do and always picked his own musicians, an attitude inherited from his father.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: No. And that is, I think, something I inherited from Dad, 'cause I never think of talk a lot.
I believe that men are men and I judge men by their actions, you see. That's the way I have always felt. That's the way I have always acted in my professional activities.

You see, I've had -- under certain circumstances, some of the boys have asked me, 'Why don't you take so and so, and so and so.' And I said, 'No, I take so and so and so and so, because I want so and so.'
You see. And that happens -- I have been not ostracized, but almost, on account of that, you see.
You see, you realize that the majority of the musicians I've had with me were just men. That's the way I consider it.
They acted towards me too, as men and I acted towards them -- I had that, as though it were a little fluid or something that
drew me to them, in both ways, and vice-versa you see, --
Because there was a personal feeling.
Yes, a personal feeling. And I'll just give you a little example.
